problem: Object-goal visual navigation DRL methods are evaluated only by target-reaching success, ignoring collisions, so policies can collide often yet score high. Directly adding collision penalties to the reward makes policies overly conservative and hurts exploration and success.
motivation: Collisions can damage robots and environments, so real deployment needs collision-aware evaluation and training. The authors observe that penalizing collisions from the start suppresses exploration, while learning to predict collisions first and then using that prediction can preserve exploration and add safety.
key_idea: Introduce the CF-SR/CF-SPL metrics and a two-stage A3C training scheme: first explore freely while learning an RGB-based collision predictor, then freeze it, feed its probability to the policy and add a collision penalty.
insight: The staged schedule matters most: Stage Only (penalty in stage 2, no predictor) gives +3.3 CF-SR on L-sTDE, versus +0.3 for CP Only (predictor trained throughout, no penalty). CP Only reaches >80% CF-SR in training but barely improves on the test set, which the authors attribute to overfitting to near-perfect training-time predictions. Freezing the predictor after stage 1 and combining it with the penalty gives the best result (+5.3). Reward-only baselines stay conservative (<2 point gains).
method: CF-SR / CF-SPL metrics: an episode counts as successful only if Done is executed with the target visible within 1.5 m and no collision occurred; CF-SPL weights this by path efficiency.

Collision prediction module: two-layer LSTM (hidden 512) on the RGB image and previous action outputs the probability of collision if MoveAhead is taken; trained with cross-entropy on MoveAhead steps.

Policy augmentation: the predicted probability p_hat is concatenated to the policy input, giving pi(a|I,g,p_hat); it is a plug-in for existing navigation models (Baseline, HOZ, L-sTDE, AKGVP, MJOLNIR-r, TDANet).
Stage 1 (1M episodes): original reward only, no collision penalty, p_hat input set to 0; the predictor learns from collision signals along the agent's exploratory trajectories.
Stage 2 (2M episodes): predictor frozen, p_hat fed to policy, reward r_o + r_c with r_c=-0.5 upon collision.
Training: A3C with 32 asynchronous agents, Adam lr 1e-4, five independent runs reported as mean±std.

setting.backbone: Existing navigation policies (Baseline, HOZ, L-sTDE, AKGVP, MJOLNIR-r, TDANet) trained from scratch with A3C plus an added 2-layer LSTM collision predictor
setting.training_data: AI2-THOR self-generated RL episodes: 3M episodes (1M stage 1 + 2M stage 2); scenes are 80 training rooms from the offline data of AKGVP / MJOLNIR; no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (plus target object label/embedding); LiDAR-based collision sensing on the real robot
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveAhead 0.25 m, RotateLeft/Right 45°, LookUp/Down 30°, Done
setting.privileged: Collision state from the environment as a training supervision signal; in real-world tests LiDAR collision sensing is used at deployment

numbers.extra: CF-SR/CF-SPL metrics (collision counts as failure); 3M training episodes; mean of 5 runs

numbers.backbone: TDANet + collision predictor trained in sim, no fine-tuning
numbers.extra: LiDAR-based collision sensing at deployment; sim-to-real

numbers_note: Own-method Baseline and HOZ variants are also in Table 1 (CF-SR 59.3 and 60.2). No standard SR/SPL without the collision constraint is reported. The paper uses custom AI2-THOR benchmarks, not the canonical list.
results: The two-stage method improves CF-SR and CF-SPL for all six navigation models (e.g. +5.3 CF-SR for L-sTDE, +3.9 for AKGVP, +8.5 for MJOLNIR-r, +7.0 for TDANet). It beats reward-only, Xiao et al. and Wu et al. collision-avoidance baselines (all <2 point CF-SR gain). In real-world tests with TDANet, CF-SR rises from 0/15 to 12/15 (80%).
limitations: Real-world deployment relies on LiDAR collision sensing because RGB-based collision prediction is unstable under domain shift, so the sim-to-real claim is only partly about vision.
Evaluated only in AI2-THOR with small gains on weaker models and a tiny real-world sample (15 trials, three scenes).
Requires 3M training episodes and a fixed stage split; the collision penalty and the stage boundary E1 are not tuned or analyzed.
